note: USB identifiers the HIL tools use to find a board's serial port (HIL-007). Keys are the ide_id of firmware/app/boards/boards.json. A board with no entry needs --port or ZPLC_SERIAL_PORT. Add an entry only from an identifier that a build or a bench run showed.

ids.source: CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_VID and CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_PID in firmware/app/boards/rpi_pico_rp2040.conf (CDC ACM shell)
CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_VID and CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_PID in firmware/app/boards/rp2040_zero_rp2040.conf (CDC ACM shell)

waveshare_rp2040_zero.note: The same identifiers as the Pico: they do not tell the two boards apart. With both plugged in, name the port; `zplc sys info` says which one it is.

ids.source: Espressif USB Serial/JTAG controller (VID 303A, PID 1001; docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32s3/api-guides/usb-serial-jtag-console.html, OpenOCD esp_usb_jtag); the shell is on it: zephyr,shell-uart = &usb_serial in firmware/app/boards/esp32s3_devkitc_esp32s3_procpu.overlay

esp32s3_devkitc.note: Not yet seen on a bench run (HIL-014). The board's other USB port (a UART bridge, 10C4:EA60 on the DevKitC-1) carries no shell, so it is not listed. After a flash the port re-enumerates under a new name: the chain opens it only after the flash step.
